the_state_that_makes_that_true.closure_verdict: closure FAILED: no verified comparator, no selected arm, no scientific proposal

why_a_supersession_was_admissible.the_priority_that_was_got_wrong_before: a seal exists to prove a design predated its scores. When no admissible score exists, the seal protects nothing, and a rule against publishing a machine name outranks the checkability of a digest that guards nothing. The correct remedy was never to edit v1 in place and never to keep the name: it was to withdraw v1 by digest and seal v2

the_three_refusal_reasons_of_the_previou.1_editing_the_published_copy_breaks_its_: TRUE, and that is why v1 was NOT edited. It was withdrawn and replaced by a design whose own digest recomputes over its own body. Nothing in this directory now claims a digest it does not have
the_three_refusal_reasons_of_the_previou.2_editing_tools_df_e1_block_py_makes_val: TRUE OF V1 ONLY, and measured: of the FOURTEEN committed design records in this repository that pin `source_code.df_e1_block.py` (thirteen sealed block designs plus RP82/fin_cost_pilot/DESIGN.json), THIRTEEN already pinned a digest the pre-edit file did not have, because that file is a living tool and has drifted many times in normal practice. v1 was the only design still matching it. So the cost of the edit was exactly one strict_code validation -- the withdrawn design's. v2 pins the repaired file and validates with strict_code=True, so the block's two unstarted W1440 FULL-DEPTH arms remain runnable, which was the stated worry
the_three_refusal_reasons_of_the_previou.3_a_design_is_never_re_sealed_after_a_sc: the rule holds, and it is not what happened. v1 is not re-sealed: it is withdrawn, by digest, in this file, and the twelve fits are NOT re-bound to v2. v2 is a new seal in state SEALED_NOT_EXECUTED with no cell of its own fitted

the_twelve_landed_fits.why: every one of the twelve cell records, and REPORT.json, TABLES.md, CLOSURE_TABLE.json and UNANCHORED_MEASUREMENT_TABLE.json, carry `design_sha256` 7d0bf921... -- v1's digest. That is what they were run against and it is the truth of the artifacts. v1 is withdrawn, so their seal is withdrawn with it; they are therefore bound to no standing seal. They are NOT re-bound to v2: v2 was sealed after their scores existed, and re-binding them would be exactly the back-dating a seal exists to prevent
the_twelve_landed_fits.what_is_kept: their numbers, unaltered. The twelve MAE/MAE_z/skill rows in UNANCHORED_MEASUREMENT_TABLE.json are honest measurements on 10 020 common evaluation rows and are not touched by this correction

the_twelve_landed_fits.what_they_may_still_be_used_for: nothing may promote, select, rank or recommend on them. They already could not: closure FAILED and the disposition is HISTORICAL_DEV_ONLY

cost_basis_carried_forward.the_correction: every footprint figure this round used or published came from resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss -- MAIN-PROCESS RSS ONLY. The correct basis is the peak charged to the scope's cgroup: for long_window_own_depth's 2026-09-26 pilot that is 7.4 GiB against a declared 9 GiB cap, where the main-process figure was 7.88 GiB
cost_basis_carried_forward.labelling: kept by basis, per figure, in FOOTPRINT_BASIS.json of this directory; no figure is restated as if it were a tree peak
cost_basis_carried_forward.the_defect: tools/df_e1_block.run_cell recorded ONLY getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss as `cost.peak_rss_bytes`, with no cgroup or tree peak anywhere in the cell record. Every cost pilot that ever justified a placement from this runner justified it from the wrong basis
cost_basis_carried_forward.repair: run_cell now records `cost.cgroup_memory_peak_bytes` from memory.peak of its own cgroup (helper `cgroup_memory_peak_bytes`, None when unreadable, and a None says the cell has NO tree peak rather than silently falling back), and labels `cost.peak_rss_bytes` with `peak_rss_bytes_basis: MAIN_PROCESS_RSS_ONLY ...`. Both bases are reported side by side in the closure rows
cost_basis_carried_forward.why_the_repair_was_allowed_here: the owner's condition was: repair only if it does not touch a file pinned by a seal that must stay checkable. It touches tools/df_e1_block.py, pinned by fourteen committed design records. THIRTEEN of those fourteen already pinned a stale digest of that file and were already outside strict_code (normal drift, not caused here). The FOURTEENTH is v1, which is withdrawn by this record and must NOT stay checkable. No seal that must stay checkable is harmed, and v2 pins the repaired file
cost_basis_carried_forward.second_defect_found_and_repaired_in_the_: run_cell also wrote `cost.host = os.uname().nodename` into EVERY cell record. That one line is the machine source of the pre-existing breach: 45 committed cell.json files on origin/master carry the coordinator host name because a tool put it there, and 44 of those 45 have their blob digest pinned in a TERMINALS or CLOSURE_TABLE artifact, so they cannot now be redacted without breaking a pin. run_cell now records `cost.host_identity` -- a salted 16-hex opaque per-host id, stable across runs on one host and different across hosts, with `host_name_recorded: false` -- and `cost.host` is None. `same host or not` is still answerable; the machine is not named

why_those_are_not_rewritten: they are records of what was actually run, under v1, and they name v1's digest correctly. Rewriting them to say v2 would forge a binding. None of them carries the host name: they were redacted at publication by tools/df_e1_publish_evidence.py (REPORT.json 12 occurrences, TABLES.md 1) and their digests are not load-bearing
